summary: ```# Marvelous Designer: Half-Skirt Production Tutorial ## Introduction In this video, we will learn how to make a wave folding skirt. This tutorial covers various styles, including a uniform skirt, pumpkin skirt, and bodycon skirt. ## Initial Setup First, we create a rectangle that is the same width and length as the waistband and sew it to the waistband. Here we freeze the waistband. After sewing, we can open the model and let the board wear on the body. ## Filling the Triangle When it is worn on the body, we can see that if it is a rectangular board, when it is sewn together with the waistline, there will be a missing piece in the front and back, similar to a triangle part. So we have to fill in this triangle to make it look like a skirt. ### Using the Extension Tool To fill it in, we use the extension tool. First, click the extension line, then cut it open. After opening the arrangement point, arrange this board on the arrangement point on the side. Then, pull the shoulder strap a little bit to ensure that the board and the model do not have penetrations. ## Modeling the Waistband When you start modeling, you can put the board on your body. If we are now modeling the waistband, because the waistband is now at the waist, it is a relatively sharp corner, so the waistband will be pulled down. We need to perform a circular process on this corner. ### Converting Points After converting this point into a free curve point, we examine the model, and its overall effect will be much better. Additionally, we can also convert the two straight points at the bottom into free curve points. Typically, we see skirts where the front and back are relatively short, and the back is longer. ### Adjusting Points To achieve this effect, we just need to move this point in the process. Press Ctrl and move this point along the side of the curve. After moving the point, we can see that the structure is now front-long and back. ## Enhancing the Design Now we can notice that the overall effect shows that the bottom has clear waves, presenting a front-long and back design. If we need to make it longer or make its fold more obvious, we can continue to do this. ### Further Adjustments If the fold should be more pronounced, we can continue to use the extension tool to extend it to the front side and unfold this board. After unfolding, we need to delete the excess straight points and press 'C' to open the editor tool. After using the editor tool, drag this straight line to convert it into a curve. ## Simulation and Final Adjustments After opening the simulation, we can manually drag the board. Since the center point is still relatively deep, we need to adjust it a bit. ### Working with Lines We take the area from 0 to 2 mm and make adjustments. Select the straight line on both sides, right-click to select the inner line according to the curve. Here, we expand the number as needed; there’s no need for a three-digit number. ### Utilizing the Flip-Folder Tool Next, we use the flip-folder tool by single-clicking the mouse on the left side of the first inner line, then moving the mouse to create a reference line. To flip this reference line, single-click in the middle and double-click after completion. Many commands in our software are executed by double-clicking the mouse. ## 3D Simulation After selecting the winder, we simulate it in the 3D window. We can observe that if we follow the previous method of making a blade, directly printing this version and simulating it will result in folds. However, for our skirt, we don’t want it to fold so closely. ### Using Positioning Tools Thus, instead of printing, we simulate it directly in 3D space. After simulation, we use the positioning ball tool to rotate it to the side of the virtual model. There is no difference between the virtual models and the actual models. ## Sewing Techniques Next, we select the sewing line and right-click to activate it. We will not use the seamstress button function but instead use the sewing line or free sewing to sew. This way, it will not interfere with the seamstress. We refer to this as a "living seamstress," where the seamstress's mouth is open and not folded like before. ### Creating Inner Lines I have created more inner lines to make them more obvious. If we want to reduce the total number of seamstresses, we should avoid creating as many as 30 inner lines initially. ## Symmetrical Version Next, we press Ctrl + D to create a symmetrical version. We then sew the front and back center together. If we want to add total length here, we can't simply pull this curve. ### Panel Line Expansion After pulling the curve, the straight lines on both sides will stretch. Thus, we need to select the panel line expansion. After selecting the panel line expansion, we can set its expansion distance, which indicates the total length to be added. ## Finalizing the Design Then, select extend for the side angle. The straight line on the side will follow the original curve. After this, use the edit panel tool to double-click on a panel line, double-click again to select the entire panel line, and right-click to align it to the panel line. ### Quick Folding If you want to fold it quickly, you can temporarily print it and then unzip it. Since the part of the panel line is extended, there will be no panel line, so use the edit panel line tool to adjust the length and let them match. ## Conclusion Finally, we can reduce the particle strength first, then delete these internal lines, and double-click to briefly simulate. If you want to keep the current shape of the entire panel, select these two panels, right-click, and choose shape optimization. This way, even if we manually drag the panel, it will maintain the previous simulation effect very well. That's it for this video. See you next time! Bye bye. ```
